contracts.scope: The diagnostic report the About destination saves on the person's own action: the archive, its environment summary, its redacted session log and the consent step. Nothing else in the product writes a bundle.
contracts.clauses: rule 2, rule 3, rule 5, section 7, section 8 A to D, section 10, amendment 2026-10-29 items 2 and 3
contracts.finding: Built in the tree, not observed in a browser. The archive is FastMediaSorterForWeb-logs[-version]-yyyyMMdd-HHmmss.zip holding environment.txt and session-log.txt, stored without compression (8 A); no JSON envelope, because the product has no copy-to-clipboard diagnostic surface. environment.txt is KEY=value lines opening schema_version=1, every key from one allowlist, a value the page cannot read written unavailable (rule 2, 8 B); the product keeps no library, catalog or history, so it writes no volume-metric family, which 8 B and amendment item 3 allow. Redaction by value runs at the log sink and again at export, before any truncation (rule 3, 7, 8 C), the personal-path placeholder carries no profile name (amendment item 2), and the exchange login, server address, device token, pairing code and certificate fingerprints are redacted with no account file or identity in the bundle (section 10). The session log is an in-memory ring of the page session, tail-only with the LOG COMPACTED marker and kept_head_bytes=0 (8 D); per-session rotation does not apply, and the LOG OMITTED marker is never written because no oversized untrusted source exists. The report is generated only on the explicit command and nothing in its path touches the network (rule 5). The build stamp reads unavailable until the release packaging writes it.
